clue.text: I'm going to repeat that, despite lacking education

parts.note: I'll is the contraction of I will, a statement of intent
to iterate is to say or do again

explanation.surface: Someone vows to say it again, however unschooled they may be.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'I'm going to repeat' as I'LL ITERATE run together; 'that, despite' merely joins it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unable to read or write has had little schooling, the core sense of the word.

clue.text: Duty to give one Frenchman a job

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, a Frenchman
a post is a position of employment

explanation.surface: An obligation to find a Frenchman employment.
explanation.definitionFit: A tax or levy imposed on goods is a customs charge.

clue.text: Call for large spectacles to be given to family

parts.note: OO looks like a pair of glasses
kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: Someone demands big glasses for their relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call' is a noun: a brief visit. OO pictures a pair of glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: A short visit or chance to take part is a brief drop-by, like a social visit.

clue.text: The ardent hen needs treatment immediately

indicators.note: something needing treatment is to be worked on and changed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A passionate chicken requires medical attention right away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs treatment' is the anagram signal working on THEARDENTHEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means on the spot, at once, without delay.

clue.text: Assess what the speed is

definitions.meaning: to judge the value or quality of
a pace, as in miles per hour

explanation.walkthrough: 'what the ... is' merely frames the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaluate is to grade something; a pace is a measured velocity.

clue.text: Obey orders to set foot on the Equator

definitions.meaning: literally to put one's toes on a line

explanation.walkthrough: The Equator is an imaginary line round the Earth, so stepping on it is literally putting a toe to a line.
explanation.definitionFit: To conform to discipline idiomatically is to stand with feet at a mark; the Equator is the planet's middle line.

clue.text: He's not a striking fellow

parts.note: a man who is not handsome, or rather a worker who refuses to join the walkout and crosses the picket line

explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' suggests good looks; it means taking industrial action, and the man who works on regardless is despised by those who strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A strikebreaker is the worker who keeps working while colleagues are out on strike.

clue.text: Country makes appeal to see doctor held by US agents

indicators.note: being held by something puts it around the other pieces

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency
O is an exclamation of appeal, as in 'O Lord'
lo is an old word meaning look or see
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A nation pleads to let a doctor detained by American spies be visited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appeal' is the cry O, as in 'O Lord', and 'see' is the archaic LO, as in 'lo and behold'; 'held by' puts them and the doctor inside the American spies.
explanation.definitionFit: This South American republic is a nation bordering Venezuela and Panama.

clue.text: Monk possessing automatic rifle

parts.note: Br, short for Brother, is a monk's title
owning means having or possessing

explanation.surface: A friar has a machine gun.
explanation.definitionFit: The Browning is a make of American firearm, designed by John Browning.

clue.text: Appropriate restrictions in real estate

parts.note: proper means suitable or appropriate
ties are bonds or constraints that hold one back

explanation.surface: Suitable limits imposed on land ownership.
explanation.definitionFit: Houses and land owned are holdings in real estate, buildings and plots alike.

clue.text: Old German has nothing, but he puts on airs

parts.note: alt is the German word for old
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: An elderly German has no money yet behaves pompously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puts on airs' suggests snobbery; here it means sings tunes, as a singer of the lower female or high male part does.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer in the voice range below soprano performs airs, that is melodies.

clue.text: Record previously set by Rex and Edward is upset

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
once means formerly
R stands for Rex, Latin for king
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A record set earlier by Rex and Edward has been broken, to their dismay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set by' and 'and' just join the pieces; R for Rex appears on royal signatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Being flustered or unsettled is to be thrown off balance.

clue.text: Small piece of offal-a very small piece

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
the liver is one of the organ meats sold as offal

explanation.surface: A butcher offers a tiny portion of organ meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A splinter or thin shaving is a tiny fragment cut or broken off.

clue.text: President awards honour to pilot

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
an airman is a flyer, such as a pilot

explanation.surface: A head of state decorates a flyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awards ... to' just places the honour before the pilot. CH (Companion of Honour) is a British distinction.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who presides over a meeting or board is its head or chair.

clue.text: Leave me some biblical books — or a section

parts.note: to depart is to go away or leave
NT, the New Testament, is a group of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be left with a few books of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: A division of an organisation or store is one of its branches.

clue.text: No, when one comes to think about it

definitions.text: No, when one comes to think about it

parts.words: No, when one comes to think about it
parts.note: the word No mirrored becomes On; the phrase also means after further thought

explanation.walkthrough: Seen in a mirror the letters N-O come out as O-N, while the rest of the clue gives the everyday meaning of having reconsidered.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means after careful thought or second consideration.

clue.text: Muddle resulting from motor-cycle rally

definitions.meaning: a race over rough terrain for motorbikes

explanation.walkthrough: 'resulting from' only links the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To jumble is to mix up; a cross-country motorbike race over rough ground goes by the same name.

clue.text: Hint from a bosom pal

definitions.meaning: to suggest indirectly, as a verb

explanation.walkthrough: As a verb the word is stressed on the last syllable; as a noun on the first.
explanation.definitionFit: To insinuate is to suggest indirectly; a confidant is a very close friend.

clue.text: Compelling need to link studies and tuition

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study, so cons means studies
training is instruction or teaching

explanation.surface: An urgent need to connect learning with teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: CON for study (pore over) is a crossword stalwart; 'need to link' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Forcing or obliging someone to act is restricting their choice, so the participle means forcing.

clue.text: Died in a city in Natal

definitions.text: Died in a city in Natal

parts.note: d is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies
urban means relating to a city

explanation.surface: Someone passed away in a South African port.
explanation.walkthrough: Natal is the former South African province, now KwaZulu-Natal, where this port lies.
explanation.definitionFit: The port is the largest conurbation in the province of KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa.

clue.text: About to give in and go back

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to cede is to yield or surrender

explanation.surface: Someone is about to surrender and retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw or retreat is to move further away.

clue.text: I sent tea in exchange for a liqueur

indicators.note: an exchange swaps things round, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sent tea and got a drink back in return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in exchange' is the anagram signal, turning ISENTTEA into a sweet aniseed-flavoured spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a sweet French aniseed-flavoured cordial drunk after dinner.

clue.text: Decline to fit another detonating device

definitions.meaning: to turn down or say no
re- plus fuse: to equip once more with a detonator

explanation.walkthrough: Pronounced differently, the second reading is RE-FUSE, putting a new fuse on a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning down an offer is to say no; re-fusing a shell is giving it a fresh detonator.

clue.text: Present from the Red Cross

indicators.note: the letters are taken out from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A gift from the Red Cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift; it means in attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in attendance is to be in this place now.

clue.text: Preference for bismuth and arsenic

parts.note: Bi is the chemical symbol for bismuth
As is the chemical symbol for arsenic

explanation.surface: Someone favours two particular chemical elements.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaning or partiality towards one side is an inclination or favouritism.

clue.text: Pleasant Democrat likely to be voted in

parts.note: electable describes a candidate who could win an election

explanation.surface: An agreeable Democrat stands a good chance at the polls.
explanation.definitionFit: Something delightful or delicious is very pleasing.

clue.text: The day before getting new uniform

parts.note: the eve is the day or ... before an event

explanation.surface: On the eve of receiving a fresh school outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uniform' looks like clothing; it is the adjective, meaning consistent.
explanation.definitionFit: Level, regular and consistent all describe something smooth and unvarying.

clue.text: Those coming to ball two hours before midnight

parts.note: two hours before twelve is at ten o'clock
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Guests arriving at a ball at ten in the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: AT TEN is the time two hours before midnight; it comes before the DANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: The number of people present at an event is the turnout of those who come.
